name: Combined dorsal and palmar approach to perilunate injuries
corridor: Radially based dorsal capsular flap combined selectively with an extended carpal-tunnel exposure to the palmar carpus

positioning.text: Position supine with the arm on a radiolucent hand table, forearm freely rotatable, and the hand accessible from both dorsal and palmar sides.

setup.text: Prepare the forearm and hand circumferentially, obtain provisional reduction when safe, document median-nerve status, and confirm complete PA and lateral fluoroscopic access.

surface_landmarks.text: Dorsally mark Lister tubercle, radial and ulnar styloids, DRUJ, and third CMC joint; palmarly mark palmaris longus, wrist creases, fourth ray, and carpal-tunnel course.

incision.text: Start with an approximately 8-cm longitudinal dorsal incision from proximal-ulnar to Lister tubercle toward the third CMC joint; add an extended carpal-tunnel incision only when palmar access is required.

superficial_interval.text: Dorsally protect radial sensory branches, release EPL from the third compartment, retract second-compartment tendons radially, and elevate the fourth compartment ulnarly; palmarly elevate flaps ulnar to palmaris longus and open the carpal tunnel under direct protection.

deep_interval.text: Raise a radially based dorsal capsuloligamentous flap while preserving its radial attachment and the radiolunotriquetral insertion; through the palmar window, protect the median nerve and retract flexors to inspect volar ligaments and interposed tissue.

layers.text: Dorsal skin, retinaculum and extensor compartments, dorsal capsule, then carpus; palmar skin, palmar aponeurosis and antebrachial fascia, flexor retinaculum, median nerve and flexors, then palmar capsule and ligaments.

structures_encountered.text: EPL, second and fourth extensor compartments, posterior interosseous nerve, dorsal capsular ligaments, proximal carpal row, median nerve, flexor tendons, ulnar neurovascular bundle, and palmar carpal ligaments define the exposure.

structures_at_risk.text: The median nerve and recurrent motor branch, radial sensory branches, EPL and extensor tendons, dorsal radioulnar ligament, TFCC, intrinsic carpal ligaments, and articular cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Divide the flexor retinaculum ulnar to the median nerve over a blunt protector, preserve the radial capsular insertion, and do not injure the dorsal radioulnar ligament or TFCC near the DRUJ.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid fixed pressure on the median nerve and avoid tensioning superficial sensory branches or extensor tendons; release exposure longitudinally rather than retracting harder.

exposure.text: The dorsal window surveys the proximal row, intrinsic ligaments, and midcarpal joint; the palmar window decompresses the carpal tunnel and permits removal of palmar interposition and repair of volar injury.

limitations.text: Dual exposure increases soft-tissue dissection and is not required when stable anatomic reduction and all necessary repairs can be achieved dorsally; comparative evidence has not shown one approach universally superior.

extensions.text: Extend the dorsal incision proximally or distally as needed; add the palmar limb for irreducible volar displacement, median-nerve decompression, or palmar tissue interposition rather than using it routinely.

indications.text: Use combined exposure for selected irreducible perilunate or lunate dislocations, trans-scaphoid patterns with volar interposition, osteochondral injury, or combined dorsal and palmar ligament pathology requiring direct repair.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid the additional palmar exposure when dorsal reduction is anatomic and stable, median-nerve decompression is unnecessary, and no volar pathology requires treatment.

implant_implications.text: Plan intercarpal wires, screws, and ligament anchors so they restore carpal alignment without tethering extensor tendons or penetrating radiocarpal and midcarpal cartilage.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Confirm scapholunate and lunotriquetral relationships, capitate-lunate alignment, carpal height, fracture reduction, and safe implant position on PA, lateral, and oblique views.

closure.text: Repair the dorsal capsular flap, close the third compartment without EPL constriction or leave EPL superficial if glide is limited, and close the palmar wound without reconstituting carpal-tunnel compression.

complications.text: Complications include recurrent instability or reduction loss, median or sensory-nerve injury, tendon adhesion or rupture, stiffness, diminished grip, infection, osteonecrosis, and post-traumatic arthritis.

bailouts.text: If the lunate or carpus remains irreducible dorsally, stop forceful manipulation and add the palmar exposure to remove interposed tissue under direct vision.

procedure_applications.condition: Dorsal reduction alone is inadequate or palmar lunate displacement, median-nerve compression, osteochondral injury, or volar soft-tissue interposition requires direct access

questions.question: Which approach is generally performed first for a perilunate injury?
What are key reasons to add the palmar exposure?
questions.answer: Irreducible palmar lunate or carpal displacement, palmar soft-tissue interposition, osteochondral pathology, or median-nerve decompression.

questions.question: On which side of the median nerve is the flexor retinaculum divided?
questions.answer: On its ulnar side, over a blunt protector.
